title: Aligning LLMs with Sparse Retrieval via Adaptive Sparse Supervision
abstract: arXiv:2610.21877v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While large language models (LLMs) offer strong semantic representations, their application to first-stage retrieval incurs substantial latency and storage costs. Neural sparse retrievers such as SPLADE provide efficient retrieval but rely on relatively compact encoders with limited representational capacity. To bridge this gap, we propose an LLM-based sparse retrieval framework with input-adaptive sparse alignment. Specifically, we introduce a dynamic $\alpha$-truncation strategy that selects input-specific supervision supports based on the cumulative activation mass of SPLADE representations. This strategy guides the LLM to preserve salient lexical signals while suppressing less informative activations, without relying on a fixed support budget. translated_title: 通过自适应稀疏监督将大语言模型与稀疏检索对齐
translated_abstract: 尽管大语言模型（LLM）具备强大的语义表示能力，但将其应用于第一阶段检索会带来显著的延迟和存储成本。诸如SPLADE之类的神经稀疏检索器虽然能提供高效检索，但依赖于表示能力有限的相对紧凑的编码器。为了弥合这一差距，我们提出了一种基于LLM的稀疏检索框架，实现输入自适应的稀疏对齐。具体而言，我们引入了一种动态α-截断策略，该策略基于SPLADE表示的累积激活质量来选择特定于输入的监督支持。该策略引导LLM在保留显著词汇信号的同时抑制信息量较低的激活，而无需依赖固定的支持预算。随后的检索微调结合了对比学习、知识蒸馏和稀疏性正则化，以提升检索效果。在MS MARCO及六个选定数据集上的实验……
tldr: 该论文提出了一种基于LLM的稀疏检索框架，通过基于SPLADE累积激活质量的动态α-截断策略实现输入自适应的稀疏监督，兼顾大模型的语义表示能力与稀疏检索的效率。
en_tdlr: Proposes an LLM-based sparse retrieval framework with a dynamic α-truncation strategy that adaptively selects input-specific supervision from SPLADE representations, combining the strong semantic capacity of LLMs with efficient sparse retrieval.
